reviews.text: Chess is for nerds, but this game is like playing chess while jet skiing across a river of flame on acid. It starts out and you're like "oh that's cool my bishops can move like knights". Then you hit the hard bosses and they are spawning extra pieces and moving like 4 times each turn and you're like "wtf that's not fair". Then you assemble your combo where you can teleport a queen directly into their bank rank and explode it a blaze of kamikaze regicide. And then you realize that's just the first difficulty level.

有些技能不太好理解，比如升级的马有一种能力是 “Can always jump”，这是什么意思？ 马总是能跳？ 国际象棋的马不是本来就能跳吗，不是只有中国象棋的马才会蹩马腿吗？ 又研究了一下，这句 Can always jump，应该是指它这个马除了有额外能力之外，也有国际象棋中马原本的能力。所谓的Can always jump其实就是允许国际象棋里一样的跳法。 但是你用Can always jump这样的表述真的有点不够清晰。 当然了，你看我写的这一段，你会发现我的表述也不比他好多少，而且我还这么啰嗦。 所以这类问题有没有可能改进呢。

I am not very good at chess, despite my love of watching 100-rated players blunder their women to Chess Simp and Levy yelling about Magnus sacrificing THE ROOOOOOOOOOOOOK. I DO love me a good roguelike/lite more than pretty much anything else, though, so I figured I'd give it a shot anyway - and I have not regretted a minute of it. Even at low ascensions and having to think extremely hard about otherwise simple moves, I'm having a great time. If you've ever seen the Stockfish vs ChatGPT meme and thought it was hilarious, well, often it can feel like *you're* ChatGPT wreaking havoc on the board - making their queen into your queen, spawning knights out of the aether, and teleporting pawns across the board to do your bidding. ... and then you've gotta fight an octopus who moves every type of piece at once, or a cobra paralyzes your king, or you're in the Thunderdome with a gorilla, and all the crazy stuff proves its necessity. It's fine. You're not a coward. 100% win rate.
This is not anything like chess -- despite being the same pieces. I haven't decided if I like it yet -- but it's interesting. 3/5 stars.

I played my very first run, and got Dues Est Machina. At the end of my turn, I spend 10 energy to get 4 queens. I also got a power up that gives me 4 energy each time a queen captures, and also 3 more energy each time I lose a non-pawn. It was an infinite and exponential loop for 20+ queens each round. The final boss, Draco didn't even stand a chance. That is the sign of a great rogue-like!

Just not my thing... not worth all the money haha. but i love drawback chess.

Despite the upgrades to pieces and relics, the game is a good exercise for chess imagination. It features numerous levels of progression, which gradually increase the difficulty. The variety of bosses (e.g. Poseidon flooding the board from below, a battle in the ring, a fight against a herd of horses) also adds to the game's excitement. As a chess player, I highly recommend it.

Some boards are very bad for certain relics. I would love a game mode which allowed me to choose between 2+ enemies on different boards, perhaps with additional factors to incentivize variety, like a minor in-match penalty when taking the 2nd option (e.g. stricter turn limit or other ascension modifiers). I'm deeply familiar with ChecksMate for Archipelago, a related chess roguelite. The Rookery is ideologically satisfying in a similar way, yet incredibly expansive. I believe I will treasure this addition to the human corpus of art. An example of a particularly difficult combination would be when your pawns start on the distal end of the board, and you have Cloning Vat with Power Pawns. In this circumstance, it's quite difficult to extract most pieces from behind your pawn wall.
best chess rogue-like.

I adore this game. It has become my comfort game that I play whenever I have some time to kill. It's well-balanced, has enough scenarios to keep you coming back, and has a great number of relics that really change how you approach the game. The approach to difficulty is very gradual, with one small change every time you go up in ascension level. Some of these aren't just boring number tweaks. For instance, at least one level introduces harder AI.

I grabbed the chess themed Humble Bundle this week, and this game alone is already worth the price of admission. The music and the art are both great. The roguelite elements don't feel as punishing or luck based as they tend to be in other games and there is still enough actual chess here to keep you engaged. If you can't get the bundle, definitely pick this up.
Very nice chess variant

Received this as part of a chess-themed Humble Bundle and I think it is the best of the bunch. There are plenty of boosts/relics that (if you pay attention) can make the runs very manageable, but still challenging. Hits the narrow band (for me) of frustrating enough to be annoyed when losing a run, yet entertaining enough to want to try again.

It's really, really good. All the decisions they've made seem to have been really intelligently thought through, so that things you initially think are pointless or unbalanced turn out to be well chosen with more exploration. It actually highlights how hard it would be to make a good chess roguelike, by actually being a really good chess roguelike.
Game is pleasant. Pwn many a peasant. Works as intended. Recommended.
